title: kb_backlog and the kb MCP facades return a command's stderr warnings with an exit 0
goal: kb_backlog, kb_querylog and kb_docs return what the command prints on stderr beside stdout when it exits 0, so a warning such as backlog.py cost's left-out items reaches the agent

run:
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import kb_mcp, backlog, tempfile, pathlib
def fake(argv):
    print('total 5'); print('cost: left out ST-x', file=sys.stderr); return 0
backlog.main = fake
t = kb_mcp.kb_backlog({'command': 'cost', 'args': []})
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); pathlib.Path(d, 'w.py').write_text("import sys\nprint('ok')\nprint('warn: partial', file=sys.stderr)\n")
kb_mcp.TOOLS = d
f = kb_mcp.facade_run('w.py', [])
bad = [n for n, x, w in (('kb_backlog', t, 'left out'), ('facade_run', f, 'partial')) if w not in x]
print('stderr dropped by:', bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

clauses.clause: kb_backlog, kb_querylog and kb_docs return what the command prints on stderr beside stdout when it exits 0, so a warning such as backlog.py cost's left-out items reaches the agent

notes: review of SP-ttgcpf7o, S2: _tools/kb_mcp.py kb_backlog and facade_run read stderr only on a non-zero exit; backlog.py cost prints left-out items to stderr with exit 0 (bl_cost.py), so the tool's sums look complete.
